summary:
I found 2 concrete issues.

- P2: [gc_direct.go](/home/dev/Projects/dewdrop/.tmp/wago-gc-read-regions-public/src/core/compiler/backend/railshot/amd64/gc_direct.go:2925) does not copy a child value ID for ordinary direct `struct.get`. The planner tracks this child. The emitter loses it. Repeated child checks then do not reuse the saved check, but the function still gets the 128-byte table frame.

- P2: [gc_value_checks.go](/home/dev/Projects/dewdrop/.tmp/wago-gc-read-regions-public/src/core/compiler/backend/railshot/amd64/gc_value_checks.go:213) clears the full local-ID slice at every region barrier. Cost is `local count × barrier count`. A large valid function can make this pass very slow. Use an epoch or a touched-local list.

I found no stale-address, trap-extent, root-mask, private-home, or public ABI defect.

I made no edits and ran no tests, as requested.
